hook.line: Mariana is writing about the old regulars of La Candelaria, and her first question to each of them is the same: do you still do what you used to do, or did you quit? Spanish answers with two verbs that pull in opposite directions.
hook.en: Are you still working at the café? (to a friend)

examples.en: I still go to the gym.
I stopped going to the gym.
Are you still working at the café? (to a friend)

examples.es: Dejé de fumar hace un año.
examples.en: I stopped smoking a year ago.
Hernando is still driving his taxi.

examples.es: Hernando dejó de manejar el taxi.

rule:
Same activity, two ends.

*Seguir* plus the *-ando* or *-iendo* form: it is still going.
*Sigo yendo al gimnasio.*

*Dejar de* plus the plain verb: it has stopped.
*Dejé de ir al gimnasio.*

The glue is different. *Seguir* takes the *-ing* form straight away; *dejar* needs *de* and then *ir*, *fumar*, *manejar*.

*Seguir* changes its stem: *sigo, sigues, sigue, seguimos*. *Dejar* is regular.

With *no*, *dejar de* flips: *Simón no deja de hablar* means he never stops.
smallPrint: Teachers call these aspectual verbs: they say whether an action continues or stops, rather than what the action is.

options: I still go to the gym.
I stopped going to the gym.
I'm going to go to the gym.
I still go to the gym.
I stopped going to the gym.
I'm going to go to the gym.
Did you stop working at the café? (to a friend)
Will you work at the café? (to a friend)
Are you still working at the café? (to a friend)

options: I've been smoking for a year.

I started smoking a year ago.

Hernando is going to drive the taxi.
Hernando stopped driving the taxi.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick *sigo* or *dejé de* and type the whole sentence: *___ viviendo en La Candelaria.* (I still live in La Candelaria.)
yourTurn.why: "Still" is *seguir*, and it goes with the *-iendo* form.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick *vivir* or *viviendo* and type the whole sentence: *Dejé de ___ en Medellín hace tres años.* (I stopped living in Medellín three years ago.)
yourTurn.answer: Dejé de vivir en Medellín hace tres años.
yourTurn.why: After *dejar de*, the verb stays plain.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish, to a friend: Are you still studying Spanish?
yourTurn.why: *Sigues* is the *tú* form, then the *-ando* form.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: I stopped drinking black coffee at night.
yourTurn.answer: Dejé de tomar tinto por la noche.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: Hernando stopped driving the taxi.
yourTurn.answer: Hernando dejó de manejar el taxi.
accept: Hernando dejó de manejar su taxi.

yourTurn.prompt: Flip it: *Dejé de ir al gimnasio.* Say: I still go to the gym.
Make it about *we*: *Sigo esperando al abogado.* Say: We are still waiting for the lawyer.
yourTurn.why: *Seguimos* is the *we* form, and the rest stays the same.

pitfalls.why: Almost. After *dejar de*, the verb stays plain; the *-yendo* form belongs to *seguir*.

pitfalls.right: Dejé de fumar hace un año.
pitfalls.why: Almost. English says "stopped smoking", but Spanish needs the *de*: *dejar de*.

personal: Tell us one thing you still do and one thing you stopped doing, with *sigo* and *dejé de*.
